recommendation: Follow up in HL7/kindling/publisher generation to add universal jurisdiction consistently for canonical resources that have no jurisdiction during package generation. Human editors should also decide whether canonical examples with explicit non-universal jurisdictions are intentional exceptions or should also include universal jurisdiction.
issue_request: FHIR-38831 asked to apply universal jurisdiction to FHIR-managed CodeSystem and ValueSet resources, later clarified as all canonical resources published in the base specification, with a final Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution to update Kindling and ensure the package carries it.
initial_application: HL7/kindling commit 813b2c0e53d6808a575c9efdfe29d8f201d6e463 added KindlingUtilities.makeUniversal(CanonicalResource) and call sites across generators. The current FHIR checkout depends on a later Kindling 1.25.5-SNAPSHOT, so the original implementation path is already present through the build dependency.
additional_context: FMG minutes corroborate the 4-0-0 approval, Vocab minutes show the issue was sent to FMG, and community searches found no conflicting Zulip or Jira decisions. Current R6 and published R5 packages still contain canonical resources without universal jurisdiction; some are jurisdiction-specific examples, while others have no jurisdiction and include generated resources not backed by direct core source files.
reconciliation: Published an empty human-review audit commit. A core-only source edit would be incomplete and potentially overbroad because the approved mechanism and several remaining omissions are in external Kindling/package generation, while examples with non-universal jurisdictions need policy confirmation before being overridden or augmented.
